species.name: Tiger Shark
mustRead: blunt square-fronted snout
dark vertical tiger stripes on the flank
long trailing upper tail lobe

species.name: Mako Shark
mustRead: sharply pointed conical snout
nearly symmetric crescent tail with a keeled stalk
large black eye and metallic indigo-blue back

species.name: Whale Shark
mustRead: huge flat mouth spanning the very front of a boxy flattened head
checkerboard of white spots and lines
prominent ridges running along the flanks
species.note: mouth is terminal at the front of the head, not slung underneath like other sharks; tiny eyes sit at the corners of the head

species.name: Basking Shark
mustRead: cavernous round gaping mouth held open while feeding
gill slits so long they nearly encircle the head
pointed conical snout and a large drooping dorsal fin

species.name: Marlin
mustRead: long round spear bill
rigid pointed sickle dorsal fin at the front
stiff keeled crescent tail and cobalt vertical bars

species.name: Sailfish
mustRead: enormous sail dorsal fin taller than the body is deep, running most of the back
long thin spear bill
thread-like pelvic fins

species.name: Swordfish
mustRead: flat broad sword nearly a third of the total length
tall stiff crescent dorsal fin
no pelvic fins and a smooth scaleless body
species.note: the bill is flat and blade-like, not round like a marlin's spear

species.name: Mahi-Mahi
mustRead: blunt vertical forehead on males
single dorsal fin running from just behind the eye to the tail
deeply forked tail on a body tapering hard to the rear

species.name: Wahoo
mustRead: very elongate body with blue vertical bars
long beak-like pointed jaws
row of finlets to a stiff forked tail

species.name: Sardine
mustRead: mirror-silver flank under a dark blue back
single small dorsal fin at mid-back
deeply forked tail and large loose scales

species.name: Anchovy
mustRead: pointed snout overhanging a huge underslung mouth reaching past the eye
bright silver lateral stripe
large eye set far forward

species.name: Flying Fish
mustRead: huge wing-like pectoral fins spread out from the body
unevenly forked tail with a much longer lower lobe
blunt-nosed torpedo body

species.name: Anglerfish
mustRead: glowing lure on a stalk arching over the mouth
enormous upturned jaw of long needle fangs
round globular soft body with tiny fins

species.name: Lanternfish
mustRead: rows of light-producing photophore dots along the belly and flank
oversized eyes on a blunt short snout
adipose fin before a forked tail

species.name: Viperfish
mustRead: fangs so long they close outside the mouth, past the eyes
first dorsal ray drawn out into a long lure whip over the head
photophore rows on a slim dark body

species.name: Fangtooth
mustRead: absurdly oversized lower fangs in a huge blunt head
deep pitted grooves and ridges on the skull
short stocky dark-brown body with small eyes

species.name: Dragonfish
mustRead: long glowing barbel dangling from the chin
mouth of transparent needle fangs
eel-like black body with photophore rows

species.name: Oarfish
mustRead: ribbon-flat silver body many times longer than it is deep
crimson crest of elongated dorsal rays rising over the head
long trailing oar-like pelvic streamers and no tail fin

species.name: Barreleye
mustRead: transparent fluid-filled dome over the top of the head
tubular green eyes inside the dome pointing upward
two dark scent pits at the front that look like eyes but are not
species.note: the two spots on the front of the face are nostrils - the real eyes are the green barrels inside the clear dome

species.name: Blobfish
mustRead: slumped gelatinous face with a bulbous drooping nose
downturned frowning mouth
tadpole body with no scales and flimsy fins
species.note: the melted look is a decompression artifact; at depth it is a normal bulbous-headed tadpole-shaped fish

species.name: Gulper Eel
mustRead: enormous loose pelican pouch mouth far bigger than the body
whip-thin tail tapering to a luminous tip
pinhead eyes right at the tip of the snout

species.name: Tripod Fish
mustRead: three long stiff stilt fin rays holding the body up off the seabed
long feeler pectoral fins held forward like antennae
slim tapering body with tiny useless eyes
species.note: the stilts make it much taller than a fish silhouette suggests - it stands, it does not swim

species.name: Snailfish
mustRead: translucent scaleless tadpole body
sucker disc on the belly
fins merging into a tapering pointed tail

species.name: Deep-Sea Fish
mustRead: oversized jaw crowded with needle fangs
large light-gathering eyes
specks of photophores on a black soft body
species.note: generic name - drawn as a representative bathypelagic predator
